newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money rates steady, liquidity improved.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money rates steady, liquidity improved.

text.p: Croatian money market rates were steady to slightly lower amid improved liquidity on Friday, dealers said.
"All the fresh demand has been covered with an extra 10 million kuna left on the supply side," one dealer told Reuters.
Fresh settlements were put at 26.6 million kuna. Call money loans granted at an unchanged rate of 10 percent accounted for two thirds of the trade.
Term deals were struck at slightly lower prices with 10-day borrowings granted at 15 percent, while one-month funds were granted at a lower 14-percent.
Savings banks were granted loans at 13.5 percent for two-week deals and at 15 percent for 10-day ones.
Croatia's National Bank expected banks to increase their Lombard borrowing by the end of the day from the current 34.5 million kuna, a bank official said.
Liquidity improved as the central bank paid the banks in kuna for the hard currency it purchased from them on Wednesday.
The banks' balances rose to 456 million kuna on Friday from 428 million, after four banks lent each other a total of 677 million kuna in direct off-market trade to square their positions.
Thursday's overnight trade totalled 33.5 million kuna borrowed by two banks to maintain their mandatory reserves. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom 385-1-4557075
